item.title: World News Brief: Nov 2, PM
item.description:
Iran and the Gulf

Explosions reported on Qeshm Island (unconfirmed details). Iranian state media reported at least five heavy blasts on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, along with claims that Iranian air defenses shot down a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone and captured two smaller reconnaissance drones. The cause of the blasts, the drone claims, and online reports of unannounced U.S. operations against Iranian air defenses have not been independently confirmed. Tehran also warned it would hit U.S. bases in Europe if President Trump orders strikes. (X story summary, updated about 7:05 PM ET)

Talks: no breakthrough, but contacts continue. Iran said contacts over ending the war are continuing after the latest round of talks ended without a breakthrough (Reuters, 8:50 AM ET). Earlier, Iran warned that any renewed war with the U.S. could last longer than the previous round, after Trump said he still had more targets to "take care" of (AFP, 7:08 AM ET).

Pezeshkian says the Supreme Leader granted negotiating powers. President Masoud Pezeshkian said on state media that Supreme Leader has given the government certain powers for talks and stressed dialogue over war. Oil dropped sharply on the news, with WTI briefly falling below $100 (X story summary). Reuters reported oil sliding on U.S.–Iran deal hopes as London's FTSE 100 rose for a fourth straight day (Reuters, 4:40 PM ET).

Gulf states on edge. Reuters reports Trump's Iran threat has renewed Gulf fears of "a war it didn't choose" (Reuters, 4:35 PM ET). Gulf Arab states have reportedly warned Iran they would retaliate if it attacks their infrastructure in response to any U.S. strike, and the UAE and Qatar have run security drills (X story summary). ADNOC's CEO said nearly one billion barrels have been drained from global inventories since the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted (Reuters, 11:50 AM ET).

Israel. Former Mossad chief Yossi Cohen said he believes an eventual "targeted operation" against Iran is inevitable (Times of Israel, 11:28 AM ET). Separately, Tucker Carlson claimed the U.S. could use a nuclear weapon on Iran's underground "Pickaxe Mountain" site; this is unconfirmed and not backed by officials (X story summary).

Diplomacy elsewhere. Oman's Sultan Haitham made the first Omani state visit to China in 48 years; a joint statement urged safe navigation in Hormuz and U.S.–Iran dialogue (X story summary). Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Turkmenistan (X story summary), and exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi begins a Belgium–Germany trip Tuesday ahead of accepting a freedom prize on Nov. 7 (X story summary).

Russia–Ukraine

Deadly strike on an aid point in Zaporizhzhia. Russian bombs hit a school used as a humanitarian aid center in Komyshuvakha village. The toll has climbed through the day: AP cited Zelensky saying 18 dead (AP, 12:48 PM ET), then Reuters reported 24 (Reuters, 1:40 PM ET) and later 26, citing emergency services (Reuters, 5:45 PM ET). Zelensky called it a deliberate double-tap strike that killed rescuers and police; Russia has not commented.

New peace talks set. U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff announced U.S.–Russia–Ukraine trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11 (Kyiv Independent, 6:54 PM ET). U.S. negotiators also meet European allies, the EU and NATO in Brussels this week on security guarantees (X story summary). EU officials told the Kyiv Independent the bloc is unlikely to accept a U.S. proposal to resume Russian gas flows to Europe through Ukraine (Kyiv Independent, 10:08 AM ET).

Zelensky's Patriot offer. In a Fox News interview, Zelensky offered a one-month pause in strikes on Russian refineries in exchange for a month's supply of Patriot missiles, which Ukraine would pay for (X story summary).

Alert-app hacks. Both Ukraine and Russia said their emergency alert apps were hacked overnight, sending false warnings of air raids and chemical and nuclear attacks (Reuters, 11:55 AM ET). Zelensky later confirmed Ukraine targeted Russian alert systems in retaliation (Kyiv Independent, 6:08 PM ET).

Oleshky truce fallout. Ukraine says Russia used the six-day Oleshky humanitarian truce to rearm, while Moscow assumes Kyiv did the same (Reuters, 8:45 AM ET). The Kremlin ruled out more operations like it for now (Kyiv Independent, 12:02 PM ET).

  • Russian attacks killed 2 and injured over 30 in the past day, with power outages in 10 regions (Kyiv Independent, 10:43 AM ET).
  • Ukraine's General Staff claims a record 2,500 Russian personnel losses on Nov. 1; this is Ukraine's own figure (Kyiv Independent, 7:29 AM ET).
  • Ukrainian intelligence (HUR) says a Su-57 was destroyed in an engine fire at Akhtubinsk airfield (Kyiv Independent, 8:23 AM ET), and that Russia has adapted its Gerbera decoy drone for one-way attacks up to 1,200 km (Kyiv Independent, 11:30 AM ET).
  • Russian media outlet Verstka reports the Defense Ministry will delay troop salary payments, except for forces fighting in Ukraine (Kyiv Independent, 12:05 PM ET).
  • Russia formally left the Council of Europe's anti-torture convention (Kyiv Independent, 7:33 AM ET).

Other Conflicts

Gaza. Israeli strikes killed three people in Gaza, medics said (Reuters, 7:40 AM ET).

Colombia. A truck bomb near a military base in Planadas, Tolima, killed four people, including a two-month-old baby, and injured at least 15. Local reports blame FARC dissidents; that attribution is not yet confirmed (X story summary).

Top World News

Ebola in DR Congo. The Bundibugyo-strain outbreak has passed 10,000 confirmed cases and 5,000 deaths across eight provinces, making it Congo's deadliest Ebola epidemic; cases have been reported in Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria, and Africa CDC is urging all countries to step up surveillance (X story summary).

Press freedom. On the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, UN Secretary-General Guterres warned of rising impunity, and UNESCO reported an 86% impunity rate for journalist killings (X story summary).

Note: "X story summary" links are AI-generated summaries of posts on X and may evolve; outlet links go to the outlets' own posts.

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 2, AM
item.description:
Covering roughly 7 PM Sunday to 7 AM Monday ET. Items marked "unconfirmed" come from claims or X story summaries that haven't been independently verified.

Iran and Israel–Iran

Talks in Doha, threats on both sides. Oil fell more than 3% Monday morning, with Brent dipping below $114 a barrel, on reports of indirect US–Iran talks in Doha. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran won't move its 60% enriched uranium stockpile and wants the US naval blockade ended and sanctions relief before any deal; officials describe a draft proposal circulating and possible follow-up talks (X news summary).

At a rally in Dubuque, Iowa, Sunday night, President Trump said the US has already damaged Iran's capabilities and that the conflict would end "very soon, one way or another." Iran warned that any renewed war could last longer than the previous round, after Trump said he still had to "take care" of more targets (AFP). Unconfirmed: reports circulating on X describe discussions of post-election strikes and timing talks with Netanyahu (X news summary).

Gulf on edge. Gulf diplomats, per Bloomberg and Financial Times reporting summarized on X, fear fresh US–Israeli strikes on a better-prepared Iran could bring heavier retaliation against energy sites and Hormuz shipping (X news summary).

Tankers hit. UKMTO reported a tanker struck by two projectiles about 72 nautical miles east of Ras al-Khafji, Saudi Arabia, on Nov. 1, crew safe; a separate Mayday came from the Strait of Hormuz after another vessel was hit. Iran's IRGC Navy claimed the ships hit its naval mines on an "unauthorized route" (X news summary). Qatar also condemned an attack Friday on its LNG carrier Al Mayeda in the Gulf; all 25 crew were unharmed (X news summary).

Diplomacy. China's Wang Yi met Iranian security official Ali Bagheri Kani in Beijing Monday and urged dialogue; Beijing plans a special envoy trip to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia this month (X news summary). FM Abbas Araghchi is in Turkmenistan for a one-day visit on trade and energy (X news summary). Reza Pahlavi begins a Belgium–Germany trip Nov. 3 and will accept the Friedrich Naumann Foundation's Freedom Prize in Frankfurt on Nov. 7 (X news summary).

Israel

Post-election coalition maneuvering continues. The Times of Israel reports the anti-Netanyahu bloc won a combined 67 seats but faces a hard path to forming a government (Times of Israel). Avigdor Liberman says he'll recommend Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister and Yair Lapid for Knesset speaker (Times of Israel).

In Gaza, Israeli strikes killed at least three Palestinians Monday, per Gaza health officials, after eight were reported killed Sunday; Israel says it targeted militants and accuses Hamas of ceasefire violations (X news summary). Israeli forces pulled back from key Hebron neighborhoods after an 11-day operation that displaced more than 3,300 Palestinians (X news summary).

Russia–Ukraine

Massive drone barrage. Russia ended a roughly 48-hour assault late Nov. 1 that reportedly involved more than 1,400 drones aimed at substations, rail lines and airbases in 22 of 24 regions, causing blackouts in cities including Kyiv and Dnipro (X news summary; drone total unconfirmed). A Russian drone strike near a vocational school dormitory in Vinnytsia Oblast on Nov. 1 killed a 13-year-old girl and a woman and injured several children (X news summary).

Zelensky's offers. Zelensky says he's ready to meet Putin in Turkey, calling Ankara a realistic mediator (Kyiv Independent). In a Fox News interview he proposed pausing strikes on Russian refineries for a month in exchange for US Patriot missiles over that period (X news summary).

Losses and the front. Ukraine's General Staff claims a record 2,500 Russian casualties on Nov. 1 and 54,400 in October (Ukrainian figures, not independently verified). ISW has assessed Ukraine made net territorial gains in October (X news summary). Sky News drone footage reportedly shows Russian forces using a humanitarian ceasefire in occupied Oleshky, Kherson Oblast, to bring in troops and ammunition (X news summary).

Reuters published a visual investigation finding many of at least 7,000 properties listed as "ownerless" in occupied Zaporizhzhia actually have owners (Reuters). In Moscow, Novaya Gazeta says it will shut down Nov. 9 after mounting state pressure (X news summary).

Other conflicts

  • Sudan: Sudan accuses Ethiopia of letting the RSF fly drones from Assosa Airport and says new strikes hit power stations in Kassala State on Nov. 2; Ethiopia denies it, and the claims aren't independently verified (X news summary).
  • Western Sahara: The UN's 35-year MINURSO mission ended Sunday after its mandate lapsed amid a US–Russia standoff at the Security Council (Reuters; X news summary).
  • Ethiopia: Videos show unidentified armed personnel in a Tigray town near the Eritrean border amid renewed clashes; claims they are foreign mercenaries are unconfirmed (X news summary).

Top world news

  • Bulgaria elected Iliana Iotova, an ally of PM Radev, as its first female president (Reuters).
  • South Africans are voting in municipal elections (Reuters).
  • A cyber-attack hit supermarket freezers in Belgium and Sweden (BBC).
  • Riots followed a demonstration in Frankfurt on Saturday; 30 people were detained (AP).
  • US midterms are Tuesday, Nov. 3; in Michigan, Democrat Haley Stevens is defending her endorsement switch to Republican Mike Rogers (BBC).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 1, PM
item.description:
Covering roughly 7 AM to 7 PM ET Sunday, Nov 1. All times are Eastern. Items drawn from X story summaries (compiled from posts, not wire copy) are marked as such; treat them as less certain than direct outlet reports.

Iran and Israel–Iran

Trump "in no hurry" on a deal. President Trump said Washington is in no hurry to strike a deal with Iran and declined to say whether he expects the US to go back to war with Tehran after Tuesday's midterm elections (Reuters, 10:00 AM). Trump and Netanyahu reportedly spoke by phone Saturday as the US laid plans to resume strikes on Iran (Times of Israel, 9:00 AM).

Doha talks continue. Iranian and Qatari mediators held a third day of talks aimed at ending the US–Iran war (Reuters, 2:20 PM). Per an X story summary, the agenda includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz and nuclear steps, and Tehran is seeking sanctions relief, frozen assets and a reduced US military presence; Iran's Supreme Leader has reportedly ordered forces to update target lists for an immediate response to any US or Israeli attack (X story; X story). The specific demands are not confirmed by a wire.

More tanker blasts in Hormuz. Iran's IRGC Navy says two tankers "exploded" after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz (Reuters, 3:20 PM). Vessel names and casualties were not given in the post; this is the IRGC's own claim.

Iran names the Royal Navy and RAF "terrorist" groups. Per an X story summary, Iran's Foreign Ministry designated the UK Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as terrorist organizations and MI6 as hostile, calling it reciprocity for British measures against the IRGC (X story). Still not confirmed by a major wire in this window.

  • Gulf stock markets slid on Iran war worries, with Qatar the exception (Reuters, 3:50 PM).
  • Former Israeli general and opposition figure Yair Golan said Netanyahu lacks the public trust and legitimacy for a new campaign against Iran (Times of Israel, 8:26 AM).
  • Exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi begins a Europe tour Nov 3 in Belgium and Germany and is set to accept a Freedom Prize in Frankfurt on behalf of Iranians, per an X story summary (X story).
  • Videos showed young Iranians celebrating Halloween in Tehran despite bans, with reports of security forces dispersing and detaining revelers (X story). Unconfirmed.

Russia–Ukraine

Oleshky truce ends. The longest truce of the war, limited to the Kherson region and brokered with the involvement of First Lady Melania Trump, ended Sunday after Russia refused an extension, Ukrainian officials said (AFP, 5:00 PM; AFP, 4:07 PM). Before it expired, Ukraine evacuated 167 residents from the right bank of the Dnipro, including 22 children (Kyiv Independent, 6:48 PM; Reuters, 6:40 PM).

Air raid app hacked. Ukraine's air force says the public air raid alert app was hacked (Reuters, 4:45 PM). Per an X story summary, it pushed fake radiation and chemical-attack warnings before being taken offline; officials urged people to ignore them (X story).

Strikes on both sides. A Russian drone hit near a vocational school dormitory in Vinnytsia Oblast, killing a 13-year-old girl and a woman and injuring more children (Kyiv Independent, 2:10 PM). Russian attacks over the past day killed one and injured 47, leaving hundreds of thousands without power across at least four regions (Kyiv Independent, 8:55 AM; Reuters, 1:10 PM). Zelensky confirmed strikes on a Russian rocket fuel factory plus a Pantsir-S2 and an S-400 command vehicle, estimating $70 million in damage (Kyiv Independent, 10:56 AM).

Front line. Zelensky says Ukraine liberated more territory than Russia seized in October (Kyiv Independent, 8:56 AM), a Ukrainian claim not independently verified. ISW says Ukrainian forces recently advanced northeast of Borova (ISW, 10:35 AM). Per an X story summary, Zelensky said he's ready to meet Putin in Turkey and would pause refinery strikes if Russia stops hitting Ukraine's energy grid first (X story).

  • Bulgaria: Iliana Iotova, who favors dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, won the presidential runoff, exit polls show (AFP, 5:30 PM).
  • Foreign Minister Sybiha urged governments to deny entry to Russian athletes as Russia's return to international ice hockey looms (Kyiv Independent, 10:57 AM).
  • Russia's independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta says it will shut down Nov 9 after 30 years, citing repression, per an X story summary (X story).

Other Conflicts

  • Lebanon: Farmers picking olives near Israeli-occupied areas face threats, with some saying Lebanese army protection is no guarantee of safety (Reuters, 9:00 AM).
  • Israel politics: Coalition deadlock after the Oct 27 election continues; commentators are floating cross-party initiatives to avoid another vote (Times of Israel, 5:00 PM).
  • Nigeria: Advocacy groups shared reports of continuing deadly attacks on Christian communities; their death tolls come from advocacy organizations, and Nigeria's government attributes the violence to broader insecurity (X story). Figures unverified.

Top World News

  • Florida jet crash: All nine people aboard a business jet (a Learjet) died when it crashed into a south Florida neighborhood, the US transportation secretary said (AP, 4:46 PM; Reuters, 5:10 PM).
  • US–Canada: Trump floated the "concept" of a US–Canada deal including a pipeline after speaking with PM Carney (Reuters, 6:00 PM).
  • US midterms Tuesday: The Justice Department will appeal a ruling dismissing its challenge to Alaska's certification of a Senate race (AP, 3:16 PM).
  • Binance: The exchange saw about $4.7 billion in withdrawals Sunday after a $6 billion-plus hack the FBI blamed on North Korea (AFP, 2:15 PM).
  • Germany: Engineering industry workers began wage strikes (Reuters, 2:30 PM).
  • China: State broadcaster CCTV dropped a Real Madrid match after Kylian Mbappe's remarks about Mao Zedong caused uproar (AFP, 11:55 AM).
  • The crew of NASA's simulated Mars mission emerged after 378 days in isolation (Reuters, 4:00 PM).

Per an X story summary, Zelensky said he's ready to meet Putin in Turkey and would pause refinery strikes if Russia stops hitting Ukraine's energy grid first (X story).

  • Bulgaria: Iliana Iotova, who favors dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, won the presidential runoff, exit polls show (AFP, 5:30 PM).
  • Foreign Minister Sybiha urged governments to deny entry to Russian athletes as Russia's return to international ice hockey looms (Kyiv Independent, 10:57 AM).
  • Russia's independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta says it will shut down Nov 9 after 30 years, citing repression, per an X story summary (X story).

  • Lebanon: Farmers picking olives near Israeli-occupied areas face threats, with some saying Lebanese army protection is no guarantee of safety (Reuters, 9:00 AM).
  • Israel politics: Coalition deadlock after the Oct 27 election continues; commentators are floating cross-party initiatives to avoid another vote (Times of Israel, 5:00 PM).
  • Nigeria: Advocacy groups shared reports of continuing deadly attacks on Christian communities; their death tolls come from advocacy organizations, and Nigeria's government attributes the violence to broader insecurity (X story). Figures unverified.

Top World News

  • Florida jet crash: All nine people aboard a business jet (a Learjet) died when it crashed into a south Florida neighborhood, the US transportation secretary said (AP, 4:46 PM; Reuters, 5:10 PM).
  • US–Canada: Trump floated the "concept" of a US–Canada deal including a pipeline after speaking with PM Carney (Reuters, 6:00 PM).
  • US midterms Tuesday: The Justice Department will appeal a ruling dismissing its challenge to Alaska's certification of a Senate race (AP, 3:16 PM).
  • Binance: The exchange saw about $4.7 billion in withdrawals Sunday after a $6 billion-plus hack the FBI blamed on North Korea (AFP, 2:15 PM).
  • Germany: Engineering industry workers began wage strikes (Reuters, 2:30 PM).
  • China: State broadcaster CCTV dropped a Real Madrid match after Kylian Mbappe's remarks about Mao Zedong caused uproar (AFP, 11:55 AM).
  • The crew of NASA's simulated Mars mission emerged after 378 days in isolation (Reuters, 4:00 PM).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 1, AM
item.description:
Covering roughly 7 PM ET Saturday, Oct 31 through 7 AM ET Sunday, Nov 1. All times are Eastern. Items drawn from X story summaries (compiled from posts, not wire copy) are marked as such; treat them as less certain than direct outlet reports.

Iran and Israel–Iran

Trump says one or two Iranian targets remain. President Trump said Saturday the US has knocked out much of Iran's military but still needs to "take care of" one or two sites, adding that talks are "going fine" but Tehran is "not very reliable" (Times of Israel, 2:03 AM; AFP, 3:40 AM).

Tehran warns of a longer war. Iran's army said any new war could be "longer than the previous conflict" and that Trump won't dictate its duration (Times of Israel, 5:19 AM). Per an X story summary, senior officials including Mohsen Rezaei vowed retaliation against US forces "wherever reachable," and Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly ordered the military to prepare unrestricted retaliation (X story).

Iran designates the Royal Navy and RAF as terrorist organizations. According to an X story summary, Iran's Foreign Ministry on Sunday labeled the UK Royal Navy and Royal Air Force terrorist groups and MI6 a hostile entity, citing reciprocity for Britain's measures against the IRGC and UK base access for US and Israeli operations (X story, ~6 AM). Not yet confirmed by a major wire in this window.

Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents. An X story summary reports the IRGC claimed four tankers hit naval mines on "unauthorized routes," plus separate reports of a projectile strike on the Qatari-owned LNG tanker Al Mayeda and limpet mines on the Panama-flagged Louise 1. Oman evacuated 25 crew from a burning tanker; no deaths were reported, and US Central Command said main shipping lanes remain clear (X story, updated 5:20 PM Sat). Details remain unconfirmed.

Rubio at the G20. Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused Iran of threatening to blow up ships and regional energy infrastructure; the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta reportedly ended without a joint communique over divisions on Iran and Ukraine (X story).

  • Iran's army spokesman said Iran has completed purchase of Russian Su-35 fighters, with delivery awaiting the end of the war (X story).
  • A 5.0 earthquake struck about 115 km southeast of Bushehr at 4:20 PM ET Saturday, per USGS data cited in an X summary; no damage to the nuclear plant reported, and claims of a weapons test are unsupported (X story).
  • A viral claim that Pakistan's ambassador was assaulted in Tehran is false; the video shows an Armenian parliament brawl (X story).
  • Iranian security chief Rezaei claimed on state TV that Saudi Arabia's defense minister warned Israel could target Turkey and Saudi Arabia next; Riyadh, Ankara and Islamabad have not confirmed (X story). Unconfirmed.

Israel: Election Deadlock

Netanyahu's coalition fell to 53 Knesset seats in the Oct 27 election, short of a majority; another election still looks most likely unless opposition figures break campaign promises (Times of Israel, 5:00 AM). President Herzog urged party leaders to "face the reality" of the results and avoid another vote (Times of Israel, 4:58 AM). Tens of thousands marched in Tel Aviv Saturday calling for a Jewish–Arab government to replace Netanyahu (X story). Ultra-Orthodox protesters blocked roads near the IDF's Tel Hashomer recruitment office Sunday morning over the draft (Times of Israel, 4:06 AM).

Russia–Ukraine

Record Russian losses. Ukraine's General Staff says Russia lost an estimated 54,400 troops killed or wounded in October, its worst month of the full-scale war (Kyiv Independent, 5:01 AM). These are Ukrainian figures and can't be independently verified.

Refinery strikes resume. Ukrainian drones hit Lukoil's Kstovo (NORSI) refinery in Nizhny Novgorod, reportedly the third strike in three days; the regional governor said over 100 drones were downed (X story, 5:16 AM). Damage extent is unconfirmed. Ukraine restarted refinery strikes Oct 30 after a two-week pause (X story).

Energy war. Russian missile and drone attacks on Oct 30 cut power to about 200,000 households in Dnipro and over 80,000 in Kyiv; Ukraine said it struck a solid rocket fuel plant in Russia's Rostov region (X story).

Diplomacy. ISW assesses the Kremlin is refusing to budge from its 2022 maximalist demands while ignoring Zelensky's offers of large-scale frontline ceasefires (ISW, 8:16 PM Sat). Lavrov said Zelensky is welcome in Moscow with security guarantees; Kyiv remains skeptical, and US-involved talks may resume in Abu Dhabi (X story). ISW called the humanitarian evacuation from occupied Oleshky, Kherson Oblast, "remarkably successful" (ISW, 6:12 PM Sat).

Other Conflicts

  • Gaza: Israeli strikes killed at least eight Palestinians Sunday, including a child, per local emergency services, with five killed near Al-Mawasi west of Khan Younis (X story, 6:53 AM). Toll per local sources; not independently confirmed.
  • Sudan: Sudan filed a UN Security Council complaint accusing Ethiopia of allowing drones to launch from its territory; a Darfur market strike killed at least 102 people, and the UN Secretary-General condemned the attacks (X story).
  • India: Five killed in fresh ethnic violence in Manipur state (Reuters, 4:45 AM).

Top World News

  • Germany: Masked rioters looted shops in Frankfurt Saturday as large demonstrations turned violent; police used water cannon against youths throwing Molotov cocktails (AFP, 5:04 AM). Interior Minister Dobrindt called for tough penalties (Reuters, 6:40 AM).
  • Binance: The exchange resumed bitcoin and ether withdrawals after covering most of the roughly $6.3 billion stolen in a hack the FBI attributed to North Korea (AFP, 4:02 AM; Reuters, 6:10 AM).
  • US midterms are Tuesday, Nov 3, with millions already voted (AFP, 5:38 AM).
  • Bolivia declared a state of emergency over El Niño impacts (AFP, 4:30 AM).
  • Malaysia Airlines says customers may be affected by the Amadeus data breach (Reuters, 3:00 AM).

item.title: World News Brief: Nov 1, AM
item.description:
World News Brief covering roughly 12:00 PM ET Sat Oct 31 to 12:15 AM ET Sun Nov 1, 2026. These items come from X News story summaries of posts. Treat claims as reported, not independently verified.

Iran: Khamenei orders a response with no geographic limits

Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly told top commanders to update target lists covering US and Israeli assets worldwide and to prepare an immediate response, with no geographic limits, if either country attacks again. Fox News and Al Jazeera are cited. (X story, updated 11:51 PM ET; related)

  • Qatari mediators in Doha have reportedly moved US and Iranian negotiators toward phased understandings. Iran would reduce its enriched uranium stockpile and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and the US would give sanctions relief. There is no final deal. Secretary of State Rubio warned at the G20 in Atlanta about Iranian threats to shipping. (X story)
  • Unconfirmed: one report cites an Israeli official describing a pager-style plan against senior Iranian commanders. The report's credibility is disputed. (X story)
  • Iran's Mohsen Rezaei says Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman warned in Tehran talks with Turkey and Pakistan that Israel would target Turkey, and then Saudi Arabia, after Iran. This is Rezaei's account. (X story)

Russia–Ukraine: Moscow invites Zelensky and refinery strikes resume

At the G20, Lavrov said Zelensky can come to Moscow for direct talks with Putin and that his security would be guaranteed. Russia rejects neutral venues. Ukrainian reaction is skeptical, and US-involved talks in Abu Dhabi are expected. (X story)

  • On Oct 30, Ukraine resumed drone strikes on Russian refineries, including Novokuibyshevsk in Samara, after a pause of about two weeks. Russian officials report minor damage. (X story)
  • A temporary ceasefire reportedly brokered by Melania Trump allowed hundreds of people to be evacuated from occupied Oleshky in Kherson region. They traveled through Crimea and Belarus to Chernihiv. (X story)
  • Ukrainian military figures claim about 54,200 Russian casualties in October, which would be the first month above 50,000. These numbers have not been independently verified. (X story)
  • Kharkiv prosecutors are investigating drone video that shows apparent civilians under a white flag being struck. They call it a potential war crime, and both sides blame each other. (X story)

Other conflicts: Sudan and Gaza

  • Sudan: a strike on a market in Darfur reportedly killed at least 102 people. Sudan has complained to the UN Security Council that Ethiopia allows drones to be launched from its territory. Guterres condemned the strikes. (X story)
  • Gaza: sporadic Israeli strikes are reported despite the nominal ceasefire, including four deaths in Nuseirat. Widely shared aerial footage of the destruction is partly months old. (X story)

Top world and general news

  • Defense Secretary Hegseth's FORTRESS plan would have major US bases keep their own power, water and fuel for up to 90 days. (X story)
  • US gas prices remain around $4.18–$4.27 per gallon ahead of the Nov 3 midterms, after the Iran conflict disrupted oil markets. (X story)
